title: Father's instruments, not reading music, and bands he played in
summary: His father played bass violin and guitar, never read music, and played with Freddie Keppard and a cornetist; brother John was Lawrence's first teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Since your father, of course, was never interviewed by anybody, I suppose, since they began writing about jazz, I was interested if you could find just a few facts about him. Did he ever play anything except bass, do you know?
Well, yeah. He was a guitar player too, played guitar too.
You know which one he started on? Bass violin. He started on bass violin. That was his main instrument.
That's his main instrument, bass violin. But he played guitar. He played guitar too, yeah. Anything else? Well, no, that's all I remember. My father played guitar and bass violin.
Do you remember, was he a pretty good reader? That is, did he usually read music?
No, my father never was a reading musician. He never read a music.
He wasn't a reading musician. I thought maybe he was. No. No, he never did.
Did he, who was your first teacher? Your teacher?
My first teacher to my brother, John Marrero.
Oh, your father didn't teach you then? No, my father didn't teach me. John taught me. Do you remember any other bands that your father ever told that he played in?

Well, Bill, he did tell me many bands he played in. Tell the truth, I don't know whether it was Emmanuel Perez or Joe Oliver. I know he played with Freddie Keppel. He did, he was a man. He did have Freddie Keppel with him. With him and his band. Yeah, his band, yes. And he had another trumpet player. We used to call him a cornet player. That was named Nene Kwaku. Oh, yeah. That was a trumpet player. I heard it. But one time.
